modules.title: Constraints and Data Integrity
modules.goal: Enforce correctness in the database instead of relying only on application code.

topics.title: Constraints Overview
topics.simple: Constraints database me rules enforce karte hain.
topics.pro: Constraints reject invalid data at write time, protecting every application that shares the database.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks BETWEEN 0 AND 100);

topics.title: NOT NULL
topics.simple: NOT NULL missing values rokta hai.
topics.pro: NOT NULL requires a value on every row and is the only direct way to require presence.
points: It does not reject empty strings.
Add it after cleaning existing NULLs.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ALTER COLUMN name SET NOT NULL;

topics.title: UNIQUE
topics.simple: UNIQUE duplicate values rokta hai.
topics.pro: A unique constraint enforces distinct key values and creates a supporting unique index.
points: It allows multiple NULLs by default.
It is a constraint and an index.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT students_email_key UNIQUE (email);

topics.title: PRIMARY KEY
topics.simple: Primary key row ko uniquely identify karta hai.
topics.pro: A primary key is a unique, not-null constraint that identifies each row and is usually referenced by foreign keys.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT students_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);

topics.title: FOREIGN KEY
topics.simple: Foreign key child rows ko parent se jodta hai.
topics.pro: A foreign key requires child values to exist in the parent key, preserving referential integrity.
points: The parent key must be unique.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE enrollments ADD CONSTRAINT enrollments_student_fk FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES students(id);

topics.title: CHECK
topics.simple: CHECK row-level boolean rule enforce karta hai.
topics.pro: A CHECK constraint rejects rows where the expression is FALSE; UNKNOWN from NULL passes, so pair it with NOT NULL when needed.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks BETWEEN 0 AND 100);

topics.title: DEFAULT
topics.simple: DEFAULT missing value ke liye fallback deta hai.
topics.pro: A default supplies a value when an INSERT omits the column; it does not replace an explicit NULL.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE enrollments ALTER COLUMN enrolled_on SET DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE;

topics.title: ON DELETE CASCADE
topics.simple: Parent delete par child rows bhi delete hoti hain.
topics.pro: ON DELETE CASCADE automatically removes child rows when the referenced parent is deleted.
points: It can delete more than expected.

example.sql:
ALTER TABLE enrollments DROP CONSTRAINT enrollments_student_fk;
ALTER TABLE enrollments ADD CONSTRAINT enrollments_student_fk FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES students(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;

topics.title: ON UPDATE CASCADE
topics.simple: Parent key update child me propagate hota hai.
topics.pro: ON UPDATE CASCADE updates child foreign keys when the parent key changes, which is useful for natural keys.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE enrollments ADD CONSTRAINT enrollments_student_fk FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES students(id) ON UPDATE CASCADE;

topics.title: Deferrable Constraints
topics.simple: Deferrable constraint transaction ke end tak wait kar sakta hai.
topics.pro: A DEFERRABLE constraint can be checked at statement end or transaction end, which helps circular references.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE enrollments ADD CONSTRAINT enrollments_student_fk FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES students(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED;

topics.title: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
topics.simple: NOT VALID constraint ko baad me validate karo.
topics.pro: Adding a foreign key or check with NOT VALID avoids a long initial scan; VALIDATE CONSTRAINT then checks existing rows.
points: NOT VALID applies to new rows.

example.sql:
ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks BETWEEN 0 AND 100) NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE students VALIDATE CONSTRAINT marks_range;

topics.title: Adding Constraints Safely
topics.simple: Existing data clean karke constraint add karo.
topics.pro: Adding a constraint fails if existing rows violate it, so clean or quarantine bad rows first.
points: Use NOT VALID for large tables.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks < 0 OR marks > 100;

topics.title: Dropping Constraints
topics.simple: Constraint drop karne se rule hat jaata hai.
topics.pro: ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT removes the rule; dropping a unique or primary key also removes its backing index.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students DROP CONSTRAINT marks_range;

topics.title: Unique NULLs
topics.simple: UNIQUE default multiple NULLs allow karta hai.
topics.pro: A regular unique constraint treats NULLs as distinct; PostgreSQL 15+ can use NULLS NOT DISTINCT to allow only one NULL.
points: Multiple NULLs are allowed by default.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT students_email_key UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (email);

topics.title: Exclusion Constraints
topics.simple: Exclusion constraint overlapping ranges rokta hai.
topics.pro: An exclusion constraint uses a GiST index to reject rows whose values conflict under a chosen operator, such as overlapping date ranges.
points: It needs btree_gist for equality columns.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE bookings ADD CONSTRAINT no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (room_id WITH =, during WITH &&);

topics.title: Domain Constraints
topics.simple: Domain reusable constraint set deta hai.
topics.pro: A domain packages a base type with CHECK and NOT NULL rules that can be reused across columns.
points: It can add NOT NULL and CHECK.

example.sql: CREATE DOMAIN mark AS INTEGER CHECK (VALUE BETWEEN 0 AND 100);

topics.title: Constraint Naming
topics.simple: Constraints ko clear names do.
topics.pro: Explicit names make errors, migrations and drops predictable instead of relying on generated names.
points: Name primary keys and foreign keys.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT students_marks_check CHECK (marks BETWEEN 0 AND 100);

topics.title: Common Constraint Errors
topics.simple: NULL, duplicates aur orphan rows common failures hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are NOT NULL violations, duplicate unique keys, foreign-key orphans and CHECK expressions that silently pass NULL.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Zara', 101);

topics.title: Application vs Database Validation
topics.simple: Critical rules database me rakho.
topics.pro: Application validation improves UX, but database constraints are the final guard shared by every writer.
points: Enforce critical rules in the DB.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks BETWEEN 0 AND 100);

topics.title: Practical Integrity Design
topics.simple: Keys, foreign keys aur checks ko schema design me plan karo.
topics.pro: A reliable schema combines primary keys, foreign keys, NOT NULL, CHECK and deliberate cascade actions.

example.sql: CREATE TABLE enrollments (student_id BIGINT REFERENCES students(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, course_id INTEGER REFERENCES courses(id), enrolled_on DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE, PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_id));

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Constraints Overview in a production query.
interview.answer: Constraints reject invalid data at write time, protecting every application that shares the database. Key rules: They enforce rules centrally. They run on writes. They make assumptions explicit.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain NOT NULL in a production query.
interview.answer: NOT NULL requires a value on every row and is the only direct way to require presence. Key rules: It rejects NULL. It does not reject empty strings. Add it after cleaning existing NULLs.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain UNIQUE in a production query.
interview.answer: A unique constraint enforces distinct key values and creates a supporting unique index. Key rules: It allows multiple NULLs by default. It supports composite keys. It is a constraint and an index.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain PRIMARY KEY in a production query.
interview.answer: A primary key is a unique, not-null constraint that identifies each row and is usually referenced by foreign keys. Key rules: Unique and not null. One per table. It creates an index.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain FOREIGN KEY in a production query.
interview.answer: A foreign key requires child values to exist in the parent key, preserving referential integrity. Key rules: The parent key must be unique. It can cascade actions. It blocks orphan rows.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain CHECK in a production query.
interview.answer: A CHECK constraint rejects rows where the expression is FALSE; UNKNOWN from NULL passes, so pair it with NOT NULL when needed. Key rules: It rejects FALSE. NULL passes as UNKNOWN. It can use multiple columns.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain DEFAULT in a production query.
interview.answer: A default supplies a value when an INSERT omits the column; it does not replace an explicit NULL. Key rules: It applies on omission. It can call functions. It does not enforce presence.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain ON DELETE CASCADE in a production query.
interview.answer: ON DELETE CASCADE automatically removes child rows when the referenced parent is deleted. Key rules: Use with care. It can delete more than expected. RESTRICT is the safer default.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain ON UPDATE CASCADE in a production query.
interview.answer: ON UPDATE CASCADE updates child foreign keys when the parent key changes, which is useful for natural keys. Key rules: It follows key changes. It avoids orphans. Surrogate keys reduce the need.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Deferrable Constraints in a production query.
interview.answer: A DEFERRABLE constraint can be checked at statement end or transaction end, which helps circular references. Key rules: INITIALLY IMMEDIATE is the default. SET CONSTRAINTS changes timing. Only some constraints are deferrable.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a production query.
interview.answer: Adding a foreign key or check with NOT VALID avoids a long initial scan; VALIDATE CONSTRAINT then checks existing rows. Key rules: NOT VALID applies to new rows. VALIDATE checks old rows. It takes a lighter lock.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Adding Constraints Safely in a production query.
interview.answer: Adding a constraint fails if existing rows violate it, so clean or quarantine bad rows first. Key rules: Find violations first. Use NOT VALID for large tables. Validate after the backfill.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Dropping Constraints in a production query.
interview.answer: ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT removes the rule; dropping a unique or primary key also removes its backing index. Key rules: Know the constraint name. CASCADE can remove dependents. Re-adding may require a scan.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Unique NULLs in a production query.
interview.answer: A regular unique constraint treats NULLs as distinct; PostgreSQL 15+ can use NULLS NOT DISTINCT to allow only one NULL. Key rules: Multiple NULLs are allowed by default. NULLS NOT DISTINCT changes that. It is a data-model decision.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Exclusion Constraints in a production query.
interview.answer: An exclusion constraint uses a GiST index to reject rows whose values conflict under a chosen operator, such as overlapping date ranges. Key rules: It needs btree_gist for equality columns. It prevents overlaps. It is advanced but powerful.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Domain Constraints in a production query.
interview.answer: A domain packages a base type with CHECK and NOT NULL rules that can be reused across columns. Key rules: Create once, reuse often. It can add NOT NULL and CHECK. It keeps rules consistent.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Constraint Naming in a production query.
interview.answer: Explicit names make errors, migrations and drops predictable instead of relying on generated names. Key rules: Name primary keys and foreign keys. Use table_column_suffix. Document the rule.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Common Constraint Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are NOT NULL violations, duplicate unique keys, foreign-key orphans and CHECK expressions that silently pass NULL. Key rules: Read the constraint name. Fix data before re-adding. Remember NULL passes CHECK.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Application vs Database Validation in a production query.
interview.answer: Application validation improves UX, but database constraints are the final guard shared by every writer. Key rules: Validate early in the app. Enforce critical rules in the DB. Do not duplicate contradictory rules.

interview.q: Module 20 · Explain Practical Integrity Design in a production query.
interview.answer: A reliable schema combines primary keys, foreign keys, NOT NULL, CHECK and deliberate cascade actions. Key rules: Start with keys. Add foreign keys. Add checks for domain rules. Choose cascade behaviour explicitly.

logic.answer: A DEFERRABLE constraint can be checked at statement end or transaction end, which helps circular references. INITIALLY IMMEDIATE is the default. SET CONSTRAINTS changes timing. Only some constraints are deferrable.

logic.q: Module 20 · Why does VALIDATE CONSTRAINT matter?
logic.answer: Adding a foreign key or check with NOT VALID avoids a long initial scan; VALIDATE CONSTRAINT then checks existing rows. NOT VALID applies to new rows. VALIDATE checks old rows. It takes a lighter lock.

logic.q: Module 20 · Why does Adding Constraints Safely matter?
logic.answer: Adding a constraint fails if existing rows violate it, so clean or quarantine bad rows first. Find violations first. Use NOT VALID for large tables. Validate after the backfill.

logic.q: Module 20 · Why does Dropping Constraints matter?
logic.answer: ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT removes the rule; dropping a unique or primary key also removes its backing index. Know the constraint name. CASCADE can remove dependents. Re-adding may require a scan.

logic.q: Module 20 · Why does Unique NULLs matter?
logic.answer: A regular unique constraint treats NULLs as distinct; PostgreSQL 15+ can use NULLS NOT DISTINCT to allow only one NULL. Multiple NULLs are allowed by default. NULLS NOT DISTINCT changes that. It is a data-model decision.

logic.q: Module 20 · Why does Exclusion Constraints matter?
logic.answer: An exclusion constraint uses a GiST index to reject rows whose values conflict under a chosen operator, such as overlapping date ranges. It needs btree_gist for equality columns. It prevents overlaps. It is advanced but powerful.

debug.fix: Review the ON DELETE action before deleting, or use RESTRICT for protected parents.

debug.title: NOT VALID not validated
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks BETWEEN 0 AND 100) NOT VALID;
debug.fix: ALTER TABLE students VALIDATE CONSTRAINT marks_range;
debug.error: Existing violating rows are not checked yet

debug.title: Duplicate constraint name
debug.broken:
ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks >= 0);
ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks <= 100);
debug.fix: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT marks_range CHECK (marks BETWEEN 0 AND 100);

debug.title: Drop wrong table
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE courses DROP CONSTRAINT marks_range;
debug.fix: ALTER TABLE students DROP CONSTRAINT marks_range;
debug.error: constraint "marks_range" of relation "courses" does not exist

debug.title: Unique NULL assumption
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT students_email_key UNIQUE (email);
debug.fix: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT students_email_key UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (email);
debug.error: Multiple NULL emails are still allowed

debug.fix: ALTER TABLE students ADD CONSTRAINT students_email_key UNIQUE (email);
